sections.title: Very short answer questions. Answer in 30–50 words.

questions.q: What is the role (purpose) of the main document in mail merge?
questions.answer: The main document contains the text and graphics that remain the same in every copy, such as the body of a form letter and the return address. Merge fields are inserted in it, and they are filled with data from the data source to make personalised copies.

questions.q: Explain the purpose of the merge document in mail merge.
questions.answer: The merge document is the result of merging the main document with the data source. It contains one personalised copy for each record (each letter with its own name and address) and can be viewed on screen, printed or saved for later use.

questions.q: Explain the purpose of creating envelopes using mail merge.
questions.answer: Envelopes made with mail merge print each recipient's address directly on an envelope from the data source, instead of writing or sticking labels by hand. It saves time and avoids mistakes when many letters must be posted.

questions.q: Differentiate between the main document and the data source.
questions.answer: The main document holds the fixed text (the letter body) with merge fields. The data source is a separate file (Word table, Excel sheet or address list) holding the changing information such as names and addresses, one record per person.

questions.q: What is a data source in mail merge?
questions.answer: A data source is a file containing the names, addresses or other information that vary in each copy of a merged document, arranged as fields (columns) and records (rows). It can be an address list, a Word table, an Excel worksheet or an Access database.

questions.q: Differentiate between the main document and the merge document.
questions.answer: The main document is the original letter with fixed text and merge fields. The merge document is produced after merging; it has a separate, filled-in copy of the letter for each person in the data source.

sections.title: Short answer questions. Answer in 50–80 words.

questions.q: Write the steps to create a data source using a Word table.
questions.answer: (1) Open a new document and choose Insert → Table; make a table with as many columns as fields. (2) Type the field names (Name, Address, City, PIN) in the top row. (3) Type each person's details in the following rows, one record per row. (4) Save the document — the data source is ready to be used in mail merge.

questions.q: Write the steps to create a data source using an Excel worksheet.
questions.answer: (1) Start Excel and open a worksheet. (2) Type the field names in the first row. (3) Type the records from the second row. (4) Save the worksheet; it can be selected through 'Use an existing list'. (5) Or select the data, copy it, paste it into a new Word document as a table and save it.

questions.q: Write the steps to edit existing data records in mail merge.
questions.answer: (1) In step 3 of the wizard choose 'Use an existing list' and click Browse. (2) Select the data file and click Open. (3) Click Edit Recipient List. (4) Move to the record using the arrow buttons, record number or Find. (5) Change the entries and save the changes.

questions.q: Write the main uses of mail merge.
questions.answer: (1) Sending the same letter to many people, each with their own name and address. (2) Inserting variable information in the body of the letter. (3) Printing mailing labels and envelopes, and making directories, invoices and address lists; merged documents can also be e-mailed.

sections.title: Long answer question. Answer in 80–120 words.

questions.q: What is mail merge in word processing? What types of documents can be generated with mail merge?
questions.answer: Mail merge combines a main document with a data source to produce personalised copies. Main document — fixed text (letter body). Data source — changing details (names, addresses). Merge document — the result with one copy per record. Documents that can be generated: (1) form letters; (2) e-mail messages; (3) envelopes with printed addresses; (4) mailing labels; (5) directories (lists), invoices and address lists. Steps: select document type, starting document, recipients, write the letter with merge fields, preview and complete the merge.

or.q: What is mail merge? Discuss the various components of mail merge.
or.answer: Mail merge is a Word feature that merges a list of names and addresses into one document so that each person gets a personalised copy. Components: (1) Main document — text and graphics that stay the same, with merge fields such as «Name». (2) Data source — a file (address list, Word table, Excel sheet, Access database) holding the data that changes, as fields and records. (3) Merge fields — placeholders replaced by data. (4) Merge document — the final result, sent to a new document, printer or e-mail.

questions.q: What types of documents are required for mail merge? Write the steps for creating a data source in MS Word for mail merge.
questions.answer: Required documents: main document (fixed text), data source (changing information) and the merge document produced after merging. Steps to create a data source with the wizard: (1) Mailings → Start Mail Merge → Step by Step Mail Merge Wizard. (2) In step 3 (Select recipients) choose 'Type a new list' → Create. (3) Type the details in fields such as Title, First Name, Last Name, Address, City. (4) Click New Entry for each record; use Customize Columns to add, delete or rename fields. (5) Click OK, give a file name and Save (.mdb).

or.q: What is mail merge? Explain its uses and write the steps to merge a letter with a data source.
or.answer: Mail merge produces personalised copies of a document for many people. Uses: form letters, labels, envelopes, directories, e-mails. Steps: (1) Mailings → Start Mail Merge → Letters. (2) Type the letter, leaving space for the address. (3) Select Recipients → Use Existing List (or Type New List). (4) Insert Address Block / merge fields. (5) Preview Results. (6) Finish & Merge → Print Documents or Edit Individual Documents.
